importantFindings.finding: RegExp.test coerces the supplied digest to text. The normalizer then copies the original JSON value into the success object. Canonical JSON equality with that normalizer therefore fails to guarantee that a resident, compressed or transport digest is a primitive string as required by the schema. There is no final schema check before publication. The sealed child's current happy-path constructors produce strings; the parent independently promises typed validation.
importantFindings.closure: Use one exact primitive-string/64-lower-hex predicate for every dynamic digest before retaining it, or enforce the full pinned schema before publication. Check rejection of wrong JSON types at the parent receipt boundary while preserving approved scalar-only output.

importantFindings.finding: A failure during the initial native membership/lineage checks rejects real work before entered.release(), leaving exercise suspended on entered.promise. On the late path a failure prior to the cancel callback similarly leaves the cancel-entry wait unresolved. The component's finally never takes control on those paths. A host timeout/disposal can fail the case, but cannot supply the required gate releases, parent finish and component cleanup. This is a distinct failure path from the previously corrected falsy sentinel.
importantFindings.closure: Make each synchronization wait observe failure/early completion of the corresponding real work in the test-only harness. Propagate the primary rejection including falsy values, enter component finally and release/finish/await its owned work. Preserve the original successful event order and keep any harness-only reactions outside ordinary M/QA.

importantFindings.area: SPEC and QUALITY; absolute controller deadline
importantFindings.finding: The child launches clamp correctly to remaining time. Async filesystem operations and recursive cleanup lack an absolute supervisor. The success publication checks the clock on entry only, before asynchronous write, readback, link and unlink, then reports success without checking elapsed time again. A late completion can therefore count as success after 330 seconds. The seven-minute job cap is a different boundary.
importantFindings.closure: Enforce the 330-second success boundary through the final publication and preserve failure-only semantics on expiry, including a blocked cleanup or publication. Ensure any hard outer deadline and cleanup arrangement keep the seven-minute job cap and avoid promoting an incomplete or late result.
